system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID / issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of the price (**AUD 4.8m**). | 25% (**AUD 6m**). The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost; none is given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The proposed cap is below the authorised starting position, and the fallback is not approved. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 aggregate basket, with recovery only above the basket. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook levels.** The Seller’s thresholds materially narrow recovery and its excess-only mechanism is not the agreed first-dollar approach. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | 24 months for general claims; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject; counter at 24 months and confine the period to general claims.** The proposed period is an unauthorised fallback and must not spill into other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; require the separate regime.** Fundamental and Title claims must not be reduced to general-warranty protections. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this is non-waivable. | **Reject; expressly preserve the carve-out.** The Seller’s all-Claims language would improperly capture conduct that must remain outside those protections. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records, plus specific entries. | Specific fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject the general disclosures; require specific fair disclosure.** The blanket references do not identify matters with the required specificity. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry; never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. | **Reject; delete or narrowly qualify as above.** The Seller’s wording sweeps in constructive knowledge and can defeat claims merely because information was available. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. The letter says final consent and evidence of satisfied conditions are not included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer consent. | **Reject; make both consent and condition-satisfaction evidence pre-Completion requirements.** Delivery alone does not establish effectiveness or compliance with conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. The letter confirms it has not been repaid and no final security discharge is included. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release; require payout and release at Completion.** The disclosed facility remains outstanding and the proposed timing leaves debt and security exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; Seller says they are its responsibility. | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently omit them. | **Require a line item or express Seller funding, including applicable on-costs.** The disclosure confirms the bonuses are absent from the funds flow and does not resolve on-costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller says it is adequate. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not independent bank verification. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and retain the cure.** Transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, while payment and assignment are unconfirmed. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. DD-006 records an unintended email delivery and a possible 1,240 records, but no confirmed access, scope, notification duty or loss. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume neither a confirmed breach or harm nor a numeric demand is established. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without asserting a confirmed breach or quantified loss.** The available facts are preliminary and do not resolve access, scope or notification obligations. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 of renewals described as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the three renewals; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Assess the terms and treatment; do not accept automatic Debt or a deduction.** The disclosures do not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; Seller treats Tax and IP as settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket override; state category-specific treatment expressly.** The Seller’s formulation risks applying general limitations to distinct claim types. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of 100% title. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification.** The register identifies Harbourglass as holder but does not itself establish the full title position or independent confirmation. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms open; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Do not treat them as settled; continue negotiating separate terms.** The playbook records them as open and does not authorise an unlimited-liability position. |
=== END ADVICE ===
